public_rationale: In summer 2025, leading LLMs were far below specialised systems in chess, the main named domain. Chess.com's report on the August 2025 Kaggle tournament of eight leading LLMs said their playing strength was 'not even close' to chess engines. In June 2025, ChatGPT 4o lost at beginner level to a 1979 Atari chess program. Poker benchmarks from just before and after the period show the same pattern: LLMs below optimal play in January 2025, and far below a solver agent in March 2026. No evidence was found of LLMs matching specialised systems in any named domain. The claim holds on its plain reading.
limitations: Logistics and navigation were not directly verified with in-period comparisons.
The poker evidence is dated outside the summer 2025 window and is used only as context.
Chess.com's 'not even close' is a qualitative statement, not a measured rating gap.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In domains like chess, logistics, poker and navigation, LLMs are outperformed by domain-specific AI.

statement.excerpt: In many domains, such as chess, logistics, poker, navigation, etc, LLMs are no match for existing domain-specific AI solutions.

from_speaker: such as chess, logistics, poker, navigation, etc
our_interpretation: The period described is summer 2025 (June to August 2025), when the quoted essay was written.
Plain reading: in domains like his examples, general-purpose LLMs performed far worse than specialised systems such as chess engines and poker solvers.
Showing a large gap in several of the named domains is enough; every named domain need not be verified.
criteria.support_condition: Dated comparisons from summer 2025 showing LLMs far below specialised systems in chess, poker, logistics or navigation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that in summer 2025 LLMs matched or beat specialised systems in these named domains.
